text:
samir: Opening thread for NewtEmbed vetting + compact strategies. Float32 baseline recall@10=0.883 on holdout-30k. Initial compact runs: naive int6-PQ=0.777, int8=0.862. Sharing a quick dashboard: https://internal.s3/newt/embed_vet/4891122334/overview.png :chart_with_downwards_trend:

ela: Good. Which pooling and preprocessing did you use? Any layer ensembles?

samir: Pooling: pooled-mean. Normalized before indexing. Tried a small ensemble (avg last2) and a mid-dim PCA reduction too. Eval CLI below:

```
./embed_eval --model newt-embed-v1 \
  --pooling mean --normalize true \
  --quant int6 --pq-m 12 --opq 32 \
  --index hnsw --M 32 --ef_construction 200 \
  --holdout holdout-30k.jsonl \
  --metrics recall@1,5,10,silhouette,topk_preservation
```

samir: Highlights: OPQ(32) before PQ recovers a lot: int6+OPQ -> recall@10 0.835. Ensemble avg(last2)+PCA(768)+PQ -> recall@10 0.859 (close to float32 on some microcohorts) but index size +24%.

pete: Did you try mixed-bit PQ? allocate more bits to high-variance subvectors? That can be a good middle ground.

samir: Yes. Mixed-bit scheme (bits=[8,6,4] by var bucket) gave recall@10 0.846 and silhouette 0.40, efficiency better than full 8-bit. Also tried residual quant (RQ) for the top-variance chunk: RQ+PQ gave 0.849 with index size similar to PQ m=12.

noor: Cohorts? short queries, faq anchors, multilingual? Where are the gaps?

samir: Short queries (<=6 tokens) are worst hit: float32 short recall@10=0.802 -> int6+OPQ=0.748. FAQ anchors -0.035. Multilang minor ~0.01. Uploaded cohort CSV: https://internal.s3/newt/embed_vet/4891122334/cohorts.csv

eval-bot: Automated regression check complete. Flags: recall@10 delta <= -0.03 on cohorts: short_queries, faq_anchors. Status: needs-triage.

ela: Two axes to explore: model-side (ensemble or layer concat + PCA) and index-side (mixed-bit PQ, RQ, OPQ retrain). Any cheap wins?

samir: Cheap wins: normalize before PQ + OPQ retrain seeded on short-query shards recovers ~0.04 on short cohort in our small tests. Also lowering PQ m and using mixed-bit on remaining subvectors helped. However, concat-last3 precompute for corpus yields best short-query recovery (short recall -> 0.791) but index cost up ~30%.

pete: What about search-time knobs? ef_search sweep? Or lightweight reranker only for short queries?

samir: ef_search: 128->0.786, 256->0.812, 512->0.837 for int6+OPQ+m12 (latency grows ~2.2x at 512). Reranker (tiny cross-encoder) rescoring top-100 recovers most short-query gap: int6+OPQ+rerank short=0.797 vs float32+rerank 0.805, but costs CPU. Best practical path seems to be: OPQ retrain + mixed-bit PQ by default, enable concat-last2 precompute or async rerank for short-query-sensitive routes.

noor: Any experiments with QAT or distillation to make embeddings quant-friendly? That sometimes helps without index bloat.

samir: Ran a quick QAT-int6 run with contrastive + CE distill. Preliminary: QAT-int6 -> recall@10 0.853 and short_queries 0.786. Combining QAT+OPQ gave 0.863 overall and short 0.795. So QAT looks promising but training cost higher.

pete: Metrics like topk_preservation or neighbor_swap_rate? Good to track.

samir: topk_preservation@10: float32 baseline 1.0, int6+OPQ 0.82, mixed-bit 0.88, QAT-int6 0.91. neighbor_swap_rate (fraction of pairs that flipped in top10) int6+OPQ 0.027, QAT-int6 0.012.

eval-bot: Suggestion: add unit gating checks: topk_preservation@10 >= 0.88 and silhouette >= 0.38 for any int6 candidate. Flagging proposed gating in PR checklist.

ela: Rollout proposal: 1) Default compact config = OPQ + mixed-bit PQ (m tuned) for storage-sensitive endpoints. 2) Offer QAT-int8 as preferred low-latency quant option. 3) Permit QAT-int6 or RQ+PQ only if gating satisfied OR if short-query routing (concat precompute or rerank) is enabled. 4) Canary plan: 0.5% traffic, route short queries to larger-index replica when enabled. 5) Retrain OPQ on a combined shard (short_queries + recent_docs) before canary.

samir: I'll queue OPQ retrain on combined shard and two fuzz-checks: paraphrase fuzz and short-query-aug fuzz. Job ids: fj-4891122334-opq, fuzz-4891122334-para, fuzz-4891122334-short. Results ETA ~12h. Also preparing PR with cohort CSV and recommended default index params + gating rules.

pete: Nice. Please include cost/latency table for ef_search choices and index sizes for each option in the PR.

eval-bot: Scheduled jobs: fj-4891122334-opq, fuzz-4891122334-para, fuzz-4891122334-short. ETA ~12h. Marking this thread needs-triage until fuzz + OPQ retrain finish.

noor: Thanks all — looking forward to the PR. If QAT promising, we might prefer that for larger customers.
samir: Will post updates here once jobs finish. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

eval-bot: Nightly canary monitor will watch topk_preservation and short_query recall if PR merges and canary starts.
